facts: PubChem BioAssay AID 1056 uses a cell-free human TNAP enzyme-activity CDP-star luminescence endpoint; the exact protein expression construct is unspecified.
All 485 ChEMBL source records align at record level with PubChem IC50_Mean (tid 2) and qualifier (tid 1); 462 standardized compounds have usable project labels at 1000 nM.
All 494 auxiliary tid columns were classified into six same-protocol families, with zero unclassified columns.

The number of per-range fitted IC50 curves varies by source row from 1 to 21, median 1. The depth proxy has AUC 0.8785 and point-biserial r 0.4949 against the project hit label. It is not the number of concentration points or verified independent repeats.

For depth-one source rows, 73 exact IC50 values were supported by available dose-response series having 7 to 10 distinct concentrations; 184 compounds had censored-only qualifiers. This is a measurement-effort and selection-bias limitation, not proof of direct binding.
packets.name: TNAP

facts: Patent US8835472B2 describes human ACC2 with the N-terminal 128 amino acids removed, insect-cell expression, and an NADH-coupled ADP enzyme-activity readout.
A preselected six-hit/six-nonhit sample matched patent example identifiers and IC50 values after nM/uM conversion in all 12 cases.

Independent comparison of patent structure drawings against ChEMBL SMILES is incomplete. Patent example 4.28 reports [M+H]+ 361 whereas the ChEMBL structure implies approximately 362.211; whether this reflects a typo, imported structure error, or identity mismatch is unresolved.
packets.name: ACC2

facts: Patent US9926281B2 section 3.5 and Table VIII describe a human TACE/ADAM17 fluorogenic peptide enzyme-activity IC50 assay with ten-point dose response.
A preselected six-hit/six-nonhit sample matched patent example identifiers, relations, and IC50 values in all 12 cases.

Three ChEMBL source compounds each map to two patent example numbers. Independent matching of the twelve patent structures to ChEMBL SMILES, including stereochemical identity of those pairs, is incomplete.
packets.name: TACE

facts: ChEMBL 37 single-assay numeric, conflict, and structural diversity checks passed in the saved review.

The source is described as Roche-donated supplemental screening data. Its available metadata only states inhibition of CPT2, without the specific protein preparation, method, or original record-level source table.
An associated 2011 Perspective article cannot by itself establish the method or provenance of the donated assay records.
packets.name: CPT2

facts: Patent US11555012B2 describes recombinant human ACLY activity measured with ADP-Glo, but Table 11 presents IC50 intervals A (<0.050 uM), B (0.050 to <0.50 uM), C (0.50 to <20 uM), and D (>=20 uM), not exact per-compound values.

ChEMBL's apparent exact 275 nM and 10250 nM values strongly resemble interval midpoints. The C interval crosses the project's 1000 nM threshold and cannot be assigned a measured hit or nonhit without molecule-level source reconstruction.
The provisional 106/360 classes are based on database display values and are not validated source-level labels.
packets.name: ACLY

facts: The saved assay description is 'TBD: TBD'; type B, mapping confidence 9, single-protein BAO label. The source document is BindingDB-imported patent US-10323029-B2 and has no DOI or PubMed ID.

The patent has S1P1-related AA IC50 tables and discusses agonist and antagonist effects, but the exact measurement method, receptor construct, and record-to-table mapping for this ChEMBL assay have not been established.
Preview/source review yields approximately 293 provisional usable compound identities, with 52 hit and 241 nonhit support at the project's threshold; these counts do not resolve the AA IC50 endpoint.
packets.name: S1PR1
